Revised assessment: The statement is mildly positive overall—“progress on vaccinations” and “strong policy support” point to strengthening activity and employment—yet clearly tempered by “inflation is elevated” and explicit references to ongoing risks. The policy mix (zero lower bound for the funds rate with a gradual taper of asset purchases) is consistent with forward guidance and QE transmission through expectations and term premia, as emphasized in Woodford and in Svensson and Woodford’s inflation-forecast targeting framework; the average-inflation-targeting language aims to anchor expectations around 2 percent over time. At the same time, Clarida’s work on the Taylor principle cautions that if inflation pressure persists, policy must eventually respond more than one-for-one, which moderates the upbeat tone. Moreover, evidence summarized in the literature that QE has limited effects on real growth compared with rate policy also tempers the optimism from continued asset purchases. Netting these forces, the tone is supportive but cautious.
